jobs.title: Executive Director at Advocates for Children of New York
jobs.description:
Advocates for Children of New York (AFC) strives to ensure a high-quality education for New York students who face barriers to academic success, focusing on students who face obstacles in their learning and students from low-income backgrounds.

About The Organization

Of the over 1 million students enrolled in New York City public schools, over 20% are classified as needing special education services, and 72% live in poverty. A staggering number of these students need additional assistance or support to succeed academically, forcing their families to navigate complicated systems to access those resources.

Our vision is that all New York City students receive the education they need to maximize their potential as adults. Since 1971, AFC has served New York City students from birth through age 26, focusing on students from low-income backgrounds who are struggling in school or experiencing school discrimination of any kind, including suspensions, inappropriate class placement, or denial of necessary services.

No matter what challenges a child and their family face, we advise them regarding their specific situation and work with the family to ensure that they receive the educational services they are legally entitled to. In 2025-26, we provided assistance in nearly 6,700 education-related matters for over 5,000 unique clients. Our workshops trained more than 9,000 families, educators, and professionals to protect students' educational rights.

AFC works side by side with families and students, providing the guidance to navigate complex systems and advocating for their needs, while pressing for structural reforms that benefit all students. Our unique model uses a multidisciplinary approach that incorporates advice and legal representation for families, know-your-rights trainings and workshops, policy advocacy, and impact litigation. Our services are free for families to access.

About The Role

What You'll Do

AFC is seeking an inspirational, strategic, and mission-driven Executive Director (ED) to lead the organization to and through its next chapter. The next ED will further the organization's impact, with the goal to scale our reach and serve more New York City children and families. The incoming leader will design and execute the road map to that goal, first by aligning our operational infrastructure to support these expanded services, and fostering systems and an organizational culture that empowers our staff to deliver excellent programmatic outcomes to more families. The ED will also champion the organization externally, ensuring that AFC remains positioned as a leading voice advocating for educational justice in New York City. This is a unique opportunity to draw on over 50 years of organizational expertise and community trust while leading organizational modernization and systems enhancement to expand impact for children and families across our city.

Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To

Visionary Leadership and Strategic Direction

Develop and execute a five-year strategic plan, ensuring AFC's mission and sustainable operational and financial growth while remaining at the forefront of educational justice
Assess and prepare the organization to scale our impact, bolstering the structures and systems that support long-term sustainability
Foster a strengthened organizational and team culture that upholds our mission and values
Sustain and evolve AFC's equality and inclusion efforts (including our DEI, disability access, and other advisory groups) to enhance our ability to develop community-informed solutions
Drive strategic decision-making in areas such as fundraising, policy, advocacy, and organizational growth

Organizational & Executive Leadership

Lead as both a strategist who can articulate the vision, and a manager in a "roll up your sleeves" culture
Develop innovative operating models that increase capacity, empower programmatic and functional leads, and establish clear expectations and accountability for organizational outcomes
Authentically lead in an impassioned, high-touch, and people-centered culture, ensuring that staff continue to feel heard, valued, and supported, while centering impact and inclusivity in decision-making processes
Oversee financial planning, budgeting, and resource allocation, ensuring fiscal sustainability
Develop and maintain strong relationships with the members of the Board to ensure positive support and strategic organizational oversight, and effectively leverage their expertise to further AFC's impact, operations, financial stability and mission
Foster Board engagement, ensuring a well-rounded and diverse governing body that reflects AFC's values

Fundraising, Advocacy, & External Relations

Supervise AFC's development team to build AFC's donor base and presence in philanthropic circles to ensure long-term sustainability and impact
Partner with the Board on development strategy, including giving and donor outreach
Oversee AFC's communications team and other staff, while working with external partners, to shape public narratives and media strategy
Represent AFC in media, education policy and advocacy circles, and public speaking engagements, as a passionate and informed thought leader, boosting our organizational visibility and cementing our positions at the forefront of education policy and development public visibility and positioning AFC as a leader in education policy

Who You'll Work With

You will report to AFC's Board of Directors and supervise the organization's senior leadership team.

Required Skills And Experience

Understanding of, and a demonstrated personal or professional passion for AFC's mission to ensure a high-quality education for every New York City student
15+ years of senior leadership experience in a nonprofit providing services to low-income communities and families, preferably in education, advocacy, policy, or legal services
Exhibits AFC's values: family-centered, grounds their work in expertise, passionate about dismantling obstacles for students and families, community orientation, sees their work as an opportunity to advance justice for under-represented communities, values impact
Experience leading teams, departments, or organizations through periods of innovation; keeping the organization's mission front and center through the change that comes with innovation
A listening and learning orientation, incorporates learnings into their leadership practice
Approachable, empathetic, and collaborative leadership style; emphasizes impactful outcomes and putting values into practice
An expert in their field (nonprofit leadership, education, law, advocacy, or policy) with the credibility to lead both internally and externally and capacity to learn new subject matter areas quickly
Keen and critical eye for opportunities to improve systems and processes, track record of leading teams to achieve operational excellence
Proven external relationship building wins, ideally having cultivated major gifts, foundation funding, and corporate partnerships
Experience engaging with the media and serving as a public voice for a social-justice organization is a plus
A bachelor's degree is required. An advanced degree is a plus, but not required.
A legal background is strongly preferred but not required

The Office of the Executive Vice Chancellor and Chief Operating Officer (EVC/COO) provides strategic leadership in all aspects of the City University of New York (CUNY) operations in the University’s Central Office and 26 campuses. The EVC/COO advances CUNY’s strategic goals and long-term plans by fostering operational excellence, accountability, innovation, and service quality. This work ensures the effective and responsible use of University resources in support of CUNY’s core academic mission.

CUNY seeks an Executive Director of CUNY Operational Artificial Intelligence (AI) Strategy to serve as the principal advisor and operational strategist for AI adoption in CUNY Operations. Reporting to the Executive Vice Chancellor and Chief Operating Officer, the Executive Director will lead the development and execution of a CUNY-wide AI Operations Strategy that modernizes administrative and operational services across the University’s 26 campuses.

The Executive Director will develop a comprehensive AI governance framework that enhances efficiency, strengthens decision-making, and ensures compliance, security, and ethical stewardship of AI use in CUNY Operations. This Executive Director role will lead the strategy to equip CUNY campuses with approved AI use cases, common standards, shared configurations, and implementation guidance, while limiting the fragmented use of unapproved, standalone AI tools.

The Executive Director will collaborate across departments – Information Technology, Human Resources, Facilities Management, Finance, Procurement, and Public Safety – to embed AI-enabled workflows in existing enterprise systems, support automation, establish governance, and modernize operational processes aligned with CUNY’s mission and values.

Key duties and responsibilities include but are not limited to the following:

Strategy Development and Governance

Develop and launch a CUNY-wide AI Operations Strategy that defines priority use cases and establishes a governance and implementation plan.

About Commonfund Institute

Commonfund Institute houses the education and research activities of Commonfund and provides the entire community of long-term investors with research, investment governance information and professional development programs. Commonfund Institute is dedicated to the advancement of investment knowledge and the promotion of best practices in financial management. It provides a wide variety of resources, including conferences, seminars and roundtables on topics such as endowments and governance; proprietary and third-party research such as the Commonfund Benchmark Studies®; publications including the Commonfund Higher Education Price Index® (HEPI); and events such as the annual Commonfund Forum and Investment Stewardship Academy.

To apply online, visit our website: https://www.commonfund.org/about/careers/

This role can be based in either our New York City or Norwalk, CT office.

Background

The role of Commonfund Institute is to contribute measurably to Commonfund’s two-part mission to enhance the financial resources of our clients and to help them improve their investment management practices. The Institute is specifically responsible for: (1) conducting proprietary market research within the nonprofit sector; and (2) for communicating strategic insights on matters of governance and investment policy to trustees and investment staff of educational institutions, private foundations, nonprofit healthcare organization and other institutional investors. Commonfund Institute publishes the leading studies of the investment practices of higher education endowments, independent schools and private and community foundations. Additionally, it produces podcasts, white papers and web-based articles, and its Executive Director is a frequent spokesperson for the nonprofit sector. In addition, Commonfund Institute promotes best practices in investment policy design and execution through industry conference attendance and sponsorships as well as Commonfund-sponsored events.

Responsibilities

The primary responsibilities of the Executive Director of Commonfund Institute include:

Serving as a primary external representative and recognized industry thought leader, cultivating relationships and elevating the firm’s visibility and reputation through active participation in industry events, media opportunities and other external forums, showcasing the firm’s expertise and market leadership.
Provide strategic direction to the Institute team and be a leader throughout the firm, engaging in internal partnership opportunities to advance the mission of the organization.
Advancing the firm’s business development strategy by partnering with Commonfund sales and relationship management teams to provide expert perspectives, research-driven insights, governance advisory and thought leadership that deepen client engagement and drive organizational growth.
Publishing frequent topical podcasts, white papers, web blog posts, articles and insights that aid Commonfund clients and prospects along a broad spectrum of strategic governance, policy and investment issues.
Providing strategic oversight and subject matter expertise for the firm’s various benchmark studies, including, the NACUBO-Commonfund Study of Endowments (NCSE); the Commonfund Benchmarks Study of Independent Schools (CSIS), produced in partnership with NBOA; the Commonfund-Council on Foundations Study of Foundations (CCSF); the annual Higher Education Price Index (HEPI), helping shape the external narrative and translate results into compelling insights for the industry; and other studies.
Conducting in-depth data analysis and reporting the findings from the above studies with an emphasis on uncovering proprietary insights and learning for Commonfund’s client and prospect markets.
Providing strategic oversight of the program direction, priorities and thematic focus for the Investment Stewardship Academy, an annual 3-day nonprofit institute for 40-50 attendees focused on advanced principles of long-term asset management and governance best practices.
Leading the strategic direction for the development of continuing education programming opportunities and learning frameworks for the nonprofit sector.

The Executive Director will also conduct additional original research on various topics identified throughout Commonfund on issues ranging from investment policies, practices and strategies to issues related to nonprofits and the public sector. The individual in this position will be responsible for collaborating with both Commonfund staff and outside experts with the goal of writing articles and preparing presentations for his/herself and on behalf of senior staff based on such research.

Requirements

Minimum 10-15 years’ experience in nonprofit management, governance/public policy or similar fields; familiarity with endowment investing principles; specific experience with and knowledge of nonprofit organizations (including personal experience as a trustee on nonprofit board(s))
Four-year degree required; advanced degrees and certifications a plus (e.g., PhD, Ed.D, MBA, CFA)

Driven by faith to serve those in need, Endeavors is a national nonprofit organization dedicated to serving individuals, families, and communities experiencing crisis. With approximately 1,800 employees working across the country, the organization is supported by a close-knit, committed team with a strong focus on its people and mission.

For more information about Endeavors, please visit: endeavors.org

The Chief Communications Officer (CCO) joins Endeavors at an exciting and important moment in the organization’s evolution. Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, this leader will serve as a trusted advisor and key member of the executive leadership team, providing strategic counsel on communications, public perception, organizational reputation, and crisis response. As Endeavors continues to evolve within an increasingly complex external environment, the CCO will strengthen organizational alignment, shape a clear and cohesive narrative across the organization's diverse programs, and ensure Endeavors' mission and impact are communicated with clarity, credibility, and purpose to employees, partners, policymakers, media, and the communities it serves.

The CCO will lead an integrated communications and marketing strategy designed to strengthen Endeavors' voice, elevate its brand, and increase understanding of its work. This is an opportunity for a strategic storyteller who can move beyond tactical communications to create a cohesive narrative that connects Endeavors' many programs, clients, and areas of impact. Leading a multidisciplinary communications function, the CCO will oversee the Director of Marketing, Director of Communications, and Director of Advancement & Impact providing strategic direction, mentorship, and leadership to ensure these functions operate cohesively in support of Endeavors' mission and organizational priorities.

The successful candidate will help Endeavors more fully share and celebrate the impact of its work. The organization approaches its mission with humility and is deeply focused on the people it serves. The CCO will honor that humility while helping the organization confidently communicate its accomplishments, elevate its visibility, and ensure its impact is recognized by the audiences that matter most.

With a national workforce of approximately 1,800 employees and programs spanning multiple states and communities, the CCO will also help strengthen internal communications and connections across a geographically dispersed organization. This leader will ensure employees understand the broader Endeavors story and see how their individual work contributes to the organization's mission.

This is an opportunity for an experienced communications executive, ideally with experience in a large, complex nonprofit organization, to help shape the next chapter of one of the nation’s largest faith-based human services organizations and help define how its story is told for years to come. The ideal candidate will bring sophisticated experience in strategic communications, reputation management, and navigating complex external environments, along with a track record of executive-level leadership and the ability to translate organizational complexity into a clear and compelling narrative that inspires trust, understanding, and engagement.

Key responsibilities include:
Provide strategic leadership for Endeavors' comprehensive communications, marketing, public relations, and external affairs efforts, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and mission.

Strengthen internal communications and employee engagement across a geographically dispersed workforce, ensuring employees are informed, connected to the mission, and aligned around shared priorities.

Collaborate across departments and functions to ensure communications strategies support organization-wide priorities and strengthen alignment across Endeavors' diverse programs, entities, and philanthropic efforts.
Use data, analytics, and audience insights to evaluate communications effectiveness, measure impact, and continuously improve outreach strategies.

Mission-Driven and Relational Leader

The successful candidate will bring a genuine commitment to Endeavors' mission and embrace its faith-inspired culture, leading with humility, service, compassion, and authenticity while respecting people of all faith backgrounds. A deeply relational leader, they will have a sincere respect for the people and communities Endeavors serves and will help the organization more confidently celebrate its accomplishments and communicate its impact.

Strategic and Enterprise-Minded Communicator

The successful candidate will bring a broad, organization-wide perspective and understand communications as a strategic driver of mission impact, organizational visibility, reputation, and engagement. This leader will be comfortable navigating a complex organization with multiple programs and entities and will be able to simplify complexity without oversimplifying the work.

Compelling Storyteller and Narrative Builder

The CCO will be an exceptional communicator and storyteller with the ability to translate complex organizational priorities and human experiences into clear, authentic, and compelling narratives. This leader will connect individual programs and client stories to the larger Endeavors mission, helping audiences understand not only what the organization does, but why it matters.

This leader will be a trusted thought partner to the CEO and senior leaders, offering candid, strategic counsel while building strong relationships across the organization.

The Executive Director leads the District’s financial services division, including budgeting, accounting, payroll, purchasing, accounts payable, revenue receipting, risk management, insurance programs, debt management, enrollment reporting, and program accounting. Working across all departments and schools, this leader aligns financial resources with District priorities to maximize resources for student learning while maintaining strong internal controls and public trust.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required Qualifications

• Professional Experience: Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in financial management, budgeting, and accounting.
• Leadership Experience: Minimum of 5 years of successful administrative leadership in a school district or public agency.

Preferred Qualifications

• Executive administrative experience in an organization with an operating budget exceeding $400 million.

• Extensive knowledge of WA State public school finance, governmental accounting, enrollment reporting, and levies.

• Ethical Stewardship & Integrity: Models high personal motivation, honesty, integrity, and ethical decision-making while responsibly managing public resources.
• Collaborative Leadership: Builds trust, open communication, and positive working relationships across Cabinet, school leaders, staff, bargaining units, and community stakeholders.
• Equity & Inclusion: Advances the District’s Equity Policy by ensuring equitable allocation of financial resources, practicing cultural responsiveness, and supporting diverse student and staff populations.
• Strategic Problem-Solving: Demonstrates strong analytical capabilities to navigate complex multi-funded budgets, anticipate organizational challenges, and drive creative, fiscally sound solutions.

Advocates for Children of New York (AFC) strives to ensure a high-quality education for New York students who face barriers to academic success, focusing on students who face obstacles in their learning and students from low-income backgrounds.

About The Organization

Of the over 1 million students enrolled in New York City public schools, over 20% are classified as needing special education services, and 72% live in poverty. A staggering number of these students need additional assistance or support to succeed academically, forcing their families to navigate complicated systems to access those resources.

Our vision is that all New York City students receive the education they need to maximize their potential as adults. Since 1971, AFC has served New York City students from birth through age 26, focusing on students from low-income backgrounds who are struggling in school or experiencing school discrimination of any kind, including suspensions, inappropriate class placement, or denial of necessary services.

No matter what challenges a child and their family face, we advise them regarding their specific situation and work with the family to ensure that they receive the educational services they are legally entitled to. In 2025-26, we provided assistance in nearly 6,700 education-related matters for over 5,000 unique clients. Our workshops trained more than 9,000 families, educators, and professionals to protect students' educational rights.

AFC works side by side with families and students, providing the guidance to navigate complex systems and advocating for their needs, while pressing for structural reforms that benefit all students. Our unique model uses a multidisciplinary approach that incorporates advice and legal representation for families, know-your-rights trainings and workshops, policy advocacy, and impact litigation. Our services are free for families to access.

About The Role

What You'll Do

AFC is seeking an inspirational, strategic, and mission-driven Executive Director (ED) to lead the organization to and through its next chapter. The next ED will further the organization's impact, with the goal to scale our reach and serve more New York City children and families. The ED will also champion the organization externally, ensuring that AFC remains positioned as a leading voice advocating for educational justice in New York City. About Commonfund Institute

Commonfund Institute houses the education and research activities of Commonfund and provides the entire community of long-term investors with research, investment governance information and professional development programs. Commonfund Institute is dedicated to the advancement of investment knowledge and the promotion of best practices in financial management. It provides a wide variety of resources, including conferences, seminars and roundtables on topics such as endowments and governance; proprietary and third-party research such as the Commonfund Benchmark Studies®; publications including the Commonfund Higher Education Price Index® (HEPI); and events such as the annual Commonfund Forum and Investment Stewardship Academy.

To apply online, visit our website: https://www.commonfund.org/about/careers/

This role can be based in either our New York City or Norwalk, CT office.

Background

The role of Commonfund Institute is to contribute measurably to Commonfund’s two-part mission to enhance the financial resources of our clients and to help them improve their investment management practices. The Institute is specifically responsible for: (1) conducting proprietary market research within the nonprofit sector; and (2) for communicating strategic insights on matters of governance and investment policy to trustees and investment staff of educational institutions, private foundations, nonprofit healthcare organization and other institutional investors. Commonfund Institute publishes the leading studies of the investment practices of higher education endowments, independent schools and private and community foundations. Additionally, it produces podcasts, white papers and web-based articles, and its Executive Director is a frequent spokesperson for the nonprofit sector. In addition, Commonfund Institute promotes best practices in investment policy design and execution through industry conference attendance and sponsorships as well as Commonfund-sponsored events.

Responsibilities

The primary responsibilities of the Executive Director of Commonfund Institute include:

Serving as a primary external representative and recognized industry thought leader, cultivating relationships and elevating the firm’s visibility and reputation through active participation in industry events, media opportunities and other external forums, showcasing the firm’s expertise and market leadership.
Provide strategic direction to the Institute team and be a leader throughout the firm, engaging in internal partnership opportunities to advance the mission of the organization.
Advancing the firm’s business development strategy by partnering with Commonfund sales and relationship management teams to provide expert perspectives, research-driven insights, governance advisory and thought leadership that deepen client engagement and drive organizational growth.
Publishing frequent topical podcasts, white papers, web blog posts, articles and insights that aid Commonfund clients and prospects along a broad spectrum of strategic governance, policy and investment issues.
Providing strategic oversight and subject matter expertise for the firm’s various benchmark studies, including, the NACUBO-Commonfund Study of Endowments (NCSE); the Commonfund Benchmarks Study of Independent Schools (CSIS), produced in partnership with NBOA; the Commonfund-Council on Foundations Study of Foundations (CCSF); the annual Higher Education Price Index (HEPI), helping shape the external narrative and translate results into compelling insights for the industry; and other studies.

Leading the strategic direction for the development of continuing education programming opportunities and learning frameworks for the nonprofit sector.

The Executive Director will also conduct additional original research on various topics identified throughout Commonfund on issues ranging from investment policies, practices and strategies to issues related to nonprofits and the public sector. The individual in this position will be responsible for collaborating with both Commonfund staff and outside experts with the goal of writing articles and preparing presentations for his/herself and on behalf of senior staff based on such research.

Organizational Overview: Endeavors

Driven by faith to serve those in need, Endeavors is a national nonprofit organization dedicated to serving individuals, families, and communities experiencing crisis. Founded in San Antonio in 1969, Endeavors has spent more than five decades providing relief and support to vulnerable populations across the nation, guided by a vision of serving others and changing lives. Today, its work spans mental health and wellness, rapid response and shelter, case management, supportive services, and programs serving Veterans, military families, individuals experiencing homelessness, and communities impacted by crisis and disaster.

Endeavors has grown into a complex and multifaceted organization with a broad geographic footprint and a diverse portfolio of programs and services. With approximately 1,800 employees working across the country, the organization is supported by a close-knit, committed team with a strong focus on its people and mission.

For more information about Endeavors, please visit: endeavors.org

Position Summary: Chief Communications Officer

The Chief Communications Officer (CCO) joins Endeavors at an exciting and important moment in the organization’s evolution. Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, this leader will serve as a trusted advisor and key member of the executive leadership team, providing strategic counsel on communications, public perception, organizational reputation, and crisis response. As Endeavors continues to evolve within an increasingly complex external environment, the CCO will strengthen organizational alignment, shape a clear and cohesive narrative across the organization's diverse programs, and ensure Endeavors' mission and impact are communicated with clarity, credibility, and purpose to employees, partners, policymakers, media, and the communities it serves.

The CCO will lead an integrated communications and marketing strategy designed to strengthen Endeavors' voice, elevate its brand, and increase understanding of its work. This is an opportunity for a strategic storyteller who can move beyond tactical communications to create a cohesive narrative that connects Endeavors' many programs, clients, and areas of impact. Leading a multidisciplinary communications function, the CCO will oversee the Director of Marketing, Director of Communications, and Director of Advancement & Impact providing strategic direction, mentorship, and leadership to ensure these functions operate cohesively in support of Endeavors' mission and organizational priorities.

The successful candidate will help Endeavors more fully share and celebrate the impact of its work. The organization approaches its mission with humility and is deeply focused on the people it serves. The CCO will honor that humility while helping the organization confidently communicate its accomplishments, elevate its visibility, and ensure its impact is recognized by the audiences that matter most.

With a national workforce of approximately 1,800 employees and programs spanning multiple states and communities, the CCO will also help strengthen internal communications and connections across a geographically dispersed organization. This leader will ensure employees understand the broader Endeavors story and see how their individual work contributes to the organization's mission.

This is an opportunity for an experienced communications executive, ideally with experience in a large, complex nonprofit organization, to help shape the next chapter of one of the nation’s largest faith-based human services organizations and help define how its story is told for years to come. The ideal candidate will bring sophisticated experience in strategic communications, reputation management, and navigating complex external environments, along with a track record of executive-level leadership and the ability to translate organizational complexity into a clear and compelling narrative that inspires trust, understanding, and engagement.

Key responsibilities include:
Provide strategic leadership for Endeavors' comprehensive communications, marketing, public relations, and external affairs efforts, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and mission.
Serve as a trusted strategic advisor to the CEO and a key member of the executive leadership team, providing counsel on communications, public perception, organizational reputation, and stakeholder engagement.

Develop a cohesive organizational narrative that connects Endeavors' diverse programs, clients, and areas of impact while making the organization's complexity understandable and compelling.
Strengthen Endeavors' national brand and public profile through compelling storytelling, media relations, digital engagement, and strategic communications.
Develop thoughtful communications strategies that position Endeavors effectively within a complex and evolving public environment and ensure its mission and impact are clearly understood.
Oversee the development and implementation of the marketing strategies for Endeavors’ philanthropic efforts, internal and external events, and employment engagement activities.
Strengthen internal communications and employee engagement across a geographically dispersed workforce, ensuring employees are informed, connected to the mission, and aligned around shared priorities.
Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing communications team, fostering a culture of collaboration, accountability, creativity, and continuous improvement.
Collaborate across departments and functions to ensure communications strategies support organization-wide priorities and strengthen alignment across Endeavors' diverse programs, entities, and philanthropic efforts.
Use data, analytics, and audience insights to evaluate communications effectiveness, measure impact, and continuously improve outreach strategies.

Mission-Driven and Relational Leader

The successful candidate will bring a genuine commitment to Endeavors' mission and embrace its faith-inspired culture, leading with humility, service, compassion, and authenticity while respecting people of all faith backgrounds. A deeply relational leader, they will have a sincere respect for the people and communities Endeavors serves and will help the organization more confidently celebrate its accomplishments and communicate its impact.

Strategic and Enterprise-Minded Communicator

The successful candidate will bring a broad, organization-wide perspective and understand communications as a strategic driver of mission impact, organizational visibility, reputation, and engagement. This leader will be comfortable navigating a complex organization with multiple programs and entities and will be able to simplify complexity without oversimplifying the work.

Compelling Storyteller and Narrative Builder

The CCO will be an exceptional communicator and storyteller with the ability to translate complex organizational priorities and human experiences into clear, authentic, and compelling narratives. This leader will connect individual programs and client stories to the larger Endeavors mission, helping audiences understand not only what the organization does, but why it matters.

As CohnReznick grows, so do our career opportunities. As one of the nation’s top Professional Services and Business Advisory firms, we foster teams in Advisory, Assurance, and Tax services that value innovation and collaboration in everything they do!

We currently have an exciting career opportunity for a Managing Director - Technology Product Management to join the Global, Digital, and Cybersecurity
team.

The Head of Technology Product Management will build, scale, and lead a new, specialized product management organization. Reporting directly to the CTO, this executive will establish product management discipline across the firm's core business units and the enterprise-wide practice management platforms: Tax, Advisory, Assurance, and Enterprise Platforms
.

The successful candidate will assess the team’s resources to determine staffing needs and lead a team of dedicated Product Managers for each line of business. This leader ensures that all technology investments, architectures, and AI integrations directly accelerate business growth, streamline compliance, and deliver maximum ROI.

As Head of Technology Product Management,
this person is expected to be a h
ands-on leader and change agent who inspires confidence through execution discipline. You will set a high bar for program delivery and personally step in to lead by example for the most challenging initiatives, demonstrating solution-oriented problem solving and calm control under pressure. You should influence and collaborate effectively at all levels – from guiding project teams day-to-day to steering executive discussions on strategy, priorities, and escalations.

The Head of Technology Product Management must translate complex technical and project details into business insights, manage stakeholder expectations, and rally cross-functional teams around common goals. This leader will promote an inclusive, trusting team environment, celebrate successes, provide constructive feedback, and ensure accountability for results.

WHY COHNREZNICK?

At CohnReznick, we’re united by a common mission to create opportunity, value, and trust for our clients, our people, and our communities. Whether it’s working alongside your peers to solve a client challenge, or volunteering together at the local food bank, there are so many ways to find your “why” at the firm.

We believe it’s important to balance work with everyday life – and make time for enjoyment and fun. We invest in a robust Total Rewards package that includes everything from generous PTO, a flexible work environment, expanded parental leave, extensive learning & development, and even paid time off for employees to volunteer.

YOUR ROLE

The Managing Director _ Technology Product Management's responsibilities are as follows:

Organization Building & Leadership

Design the Org Structure: Build the firm's inaugural technology product management department from the ground up, establishing standardized methodologies, governance, and product playbooks.
Talent Acquisition: Recruit, hire, and onboard dedicated Product Managers to represent each strategic line: Tax, Advisory, Assurance, and Enterprise Platforms.
Mentorship & Culture: Cultivate a culture of high performance, continuous learning, data-driven prioritization, and user-centric design within the product team.

Strategic Product Alignment

Tax Technology Portfolio: Oversee product strategies that automate compliance, streamline complex filing workflows, and deploy predictive data analytics for tax planning.
Advisory Platform Innovation: Drive the delivery of data-heavy, client-facing consulting portals, risk assessment tools, and transaction advisory tools.
Assurance Modernization: Guide the productization of advanced audit software, secure client portals, and continuous monitoring automated systems.
Enterprise Platforms: Own the technology strategy for the core enterprise platforms including SAP, CRM, HRIS, and other key applications.

Execution & Stakeholder Management

C-Suite Bridge: Collaborate directly with the CTO and practice leaders to align product roadmaps with the firm’s growth strategy.
Velocity vs. Governance: Balance rapid solution delivery with strict professional services security regulations, data privacy laws, and compliance standards.
Metrics & ROI: Establish product KPIs focused on speed to market, operational efficiency gains, and total cost of ownership.

YOUR EXPERIENCE

The Successful Candidate Will Have

12+ years in technical product management, with 5+ years of experience directly building, scaling, and managing a team of product managers.
Deep expertise within public accounting, corporate finance, SaaS, or professional services environments.
Proven success delivering cloud-native enterprise software, advanced data analytics platforms, and Gen-AI integrated business workflows.
Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, Business Administration, Information Systems, or a related field.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience within a large professional services, consulting, or technology-driven organization is highly desirable, indicating ability to thrive in a fast-paced, client-focused and regulatory environment. Familiarity with governance in highly regulated industries (e.g., finance, accounting, government) is a plus.
Demonstrated success in leading organizational change or business transformation initiatives in an enterprise setting.
Hands-on background in software engineering, systems architecture, or IT operations is beneficial, as it enables deeper technical credibility and problem-solving in complex program contexts.

Director of Business Development

Job Overview: Responsible for the planning, construction, and execution of the company's global business development system. Focusing on cryptocurrency, digital assets, blockchain, and related fintech businesses, continuously expand institutional clients, strategic partners, ecosystem projects, and commercial channels to drive sustained growth in the company's business scale and market coverage.

This position requires over 20 years of management experience, the ability to independently formulate business development strategies, establish a mature business development system, and lead cross-regional business teams to achieve long-term business goals.

Main Responsibilities:
I. Business Strategy and Market Expansion
Formulate the company's medium- and long-term business development strategy, market entry strategy, and regional development plan.
Analyze the development trends and competitive landscape of the cryptocurrency, digital asset, blockchain, and fintech markets.
Identify new business models, business opportunities, target markets, and potential revenue streams.
Establish business development plans for key markets and key clients, and drive the implementation of the strategy.
Adjust business development direction and resource allocation in a timely manner according to market changes.

II. Institutional Clients and Business Partnerships
Responsible for developing and maintaining large institutional clients, corporate clients, financial institutions, and industry partners.

Expand cooperation resources with trading platforms, asset management institutions, payment institutions, fintech companies, and blockchain projects.

Lead negotiations for key business collaborations, strategic partnerships, and long-term cooperation agreements.

Establish a long-term relationship system with high-value clients and strategic partners.

Drive the implementation of cross-institutional, cross-regional, and cross-business line cooperation projects.

III. Business Channel Development
Establish and continuously optimize a global business development channel system.

Develop new cooperation channels, institutional channels, industry resources, and ecosystem cooperation networks.

Establish channel evaluation, cooperation management, and business conversion mechanisms.

Improve channel customer acquisition efficiency and business cooperation conversion rates.

Build a long-term and stable partner ecosystem.

IV. Team Management
Responsible for the organization, staffing, and daily management of the business development team.

Formulate annual and quarterly business goals for the team and monitor their implementation.

Establish business development processes, customer management systems, and performance management mechanisms.

Train business development leaders and core management personnel.

Lead cross-regional and cross-functional teams to complete complex business projects.

Establish standardized and replicable business development methodologies.

V. Key Project Management
Responsible for the overall advancement of the company's major business expansion projects.

Manage key clients, strategic partnerships, and large-scale commercial projects throughout the entire process.

Coordinate with product, operations, compliance, legal, technology, and finance departments to ensure project implementation.

Handle key issues and complex negotiations in large-scale commercial collaborations.

Be responsible for the commercial results, execution progress, and cooperation quality of major projects.

VI. Market and Competitive Analysis
Continuously track global digital asset and cryptocurrency industry dynamics.

Analyze competitors' business models, customer structures, market strategies, and partnership networks.

Identify business opportunities and potential risks arising from industry changes.

Regularly generate market and business expansion analyses to provide a basis for company business decisions.

VII. Business Growth and Operational Management
Establish a business expansion target, sales funnel, and commercial conversion management system.

Monitor core indicators such as customer acquisition, partnership conversion, business growth, and customer retention.

Drive business growth in key regions, key products, and key clients.

Optimize business development processes and improve overall team operational efficiency.

Continuously adjust business expansion strategies based on operational data.

Job Requirements:

Over 20 years of management experience.

Extensive experience in business development, commercial development, strategic partnerships, or corporate management.

Business management experience in large enterprises, fintech, digital assets, blockchain, internet finance, or related industries.

Experience in global market expansion and institutional client development.

Experience in negotiating, advancing, and implementing large-scale business cooperation projects.

Strong strategic planning, business judgment, and market analysis capabilities.

Extensive experience in team management and organizational development.

Ability to manage complex, multi-regional, and multi-business-line commercial projects.

Familiarity with cryptocurrency, digital assets, blockchain, trading platforms, Web3, and related fintech business models.

Strong business negotiation, client relationship management, and cross-departmental coordination skills.

Ability to develop and execute long-term business strategies in the rapidly changing digital asset industry environment.

Strong business acumen and responsibility for business growth, market expansion, and business results.
